questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Labour is defined as the process by which a fetus, after attaining ______, is expelled from the ______.
questions.exp: Labour = process by which a fetus after attaining the period of viability is expelled from the genital tract. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Which set completes the five criteria for normal labour?
opts: Spontaneous onset; term gestation (37–42 wks); vertex presentation; uncomplicated delivery; vaginal delivery
Induced onset; term; breech; forceps; vaginal
Spontaneous onset; any gestation; cephalic; C-section allowed; live birth
Spontaneous onset; term; vertex; epidural; instrumental allowed
questions.exp: Criteria: spontaneous onset, term gestation (37 to 42 wks), vertex presentation, uncomplicated delivery, vaginal delivery. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Phase 1 of labour (uterine quiescence) is characterised by:
opts: Unresponsive uterus, soft cervix, main hormone progesterone
Functional progesterone withdrawal and ↑ gap junctions
Active uterine contractions of all stages
questions.exp: Phase 1: uterus unresponsive, cervix soft, main hormone progesterone. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Phase 2 (myometrial activation / preparatory phase) includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Functional withdrawal of progesterone and ↑ estrogen
↑ oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors and ↑ gap junctions
questions.exp: Phase 2 = functional withdrawal of progesterone, ↑ estrogen, ↑ oxytocin/PG receptors, ↑ gap junctions, cervical ripening. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Match phase 3 and phase 4 of labour:
opts: Phase 3 = uterine stimulation/contraction (all stages of labour); Phase 4 = postpartum phase
questions.exp: Phase 3: uterine stimulation – all stages of labour included; Phase 4: postpartum. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Arrange the fetal cascade for onset of labour:
opts: Fetal hypothalamus (CRH) → fetal pituitary (ACTH) → fetal adrenal → DHEA-S → placental estrogen → uterine contractions
questions.exp: Hypothalamus CRH → pituitary ACTH → adrenal DHEA-sulfate → converted to estrogen in placenta → uterine contractions. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Lightening (welcome sign) is ______ leading to ______.
opts: Descent of fetal head into pelvis; ↓ fundal height and relief of respiratory distress
Onset of true labour pain; cervical dilatation
questions.exp: Lightening = descent of head into pelvis → ↓ fundal height, relieving respiratory distress. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Cervical ripening in the pre-labour state occurs due to prostaglandins and connective tissue changes that include:
opts: ↓ cross-linking of fibres, ↑ water content, ↑ hyaluronic acid
questions.exp: Ripening: ↓ cross-linking of fibres, ↑ water content, ↑ hyaluronic acid; Bishop score assesses cervix before induction. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: True labour pain contractions are ______ and ______, whereas false labour pain contractions are ______.
opts: Regular & rhythmic; progressive in intensity, frequency and strength; irregular/continuous and non-progressive
questions.exp: True: regular, rhythmic, progressive (↑ intensity, frequency, strength) → cervical dilatation. False: irregular/continuous, non-progressive, no dilatation. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Site of pain – true labour : false labour.
opts: Lower abdomen radiating to back of thigh : does not radiate
Epigastric radiating to back : lower abdomen
questions.exp: True labour pain is in the lower abdomen radiating to the back of thigh; false pain does not radiate. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Show (mucosal blood + plug) and bag of membranes – true labour : false labour.
questions.exp: True labour: show present, bag of membranes felt; false labour: show absent, membranes not felt. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Response to sedation, enema and rest – true labour : false labour.
questions.exp: False labour pains respond to sedation, enema and rest; true labour pains do not. (Book p513)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: The mnemonic '3 Ps' for requirements of labour stands for:
questions.exp: 3 Ps: Push = contractions, Passage = pelvis, Passenger = baby. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Uterine contractions – origin : speed : time to depolarize entire uterus : predominant site.
questions.exp: Origin cornua; speed 2 cm/sec; 15 sec to depolarize entire uterus; predominant contraction site fundus. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Strength thresholds – contractions become palpable at ______, painful at ______ and cause cervical dilatation at ______.
questions.exp: Palpable 10 mmHg, painful 15 mmHg, cervical dilatation 20–25 mmHg. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Contraction strength during stages – 1st stage : 2nd & 3rd stage : basal (released) tone.
questions.exp: 1st stage 40–50 mmHg; 2nd/3rd stage 100–120 mmHg; basal tone 10–20 mmHg; monitored every 30 min. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: One Montevideo unit (MVU) is calculated as:
opts: Strength of contraction (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min
questions.exp: 1 MVU = strength (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min; adequate = 200–220 MVU. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: As pregnancy advances the upper uterine segment is formed by ______ and ______ during labour; the lower segment is formed by ______ and ______; in the 1st stage the effaced cervix becomes part of ______.
opts: Entire uterus; contracts; isthmus; passively dilates; lower uterine segment
Isthmus; dilates; fundus; contracts; upper segment
questions.exp: Upper segment = entire uterus (contracts); lower segment = isthmus (passively dilates); effaced cervix becomes part of LUS. Blood flow to uterus ↓ during contractions. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Tachysystole is defined as ______ and its most common cause is ______.
questions.exp: Tachysystole = >5 contractions/10 min; m/c cause misoprostol > oxytocin. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: The consequence of tachysystole and its CTG picture are:
opts: Fetal distress due to ↓ blood supply; prolonged deceleration
questions.exp: Consequence: fetal distress (↓ blood supply); CTG shows prolonged deceleration. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Management sequence of tachysystole:
opts: Stop oxytocin → left lateral position → O2 by mask → IV fluids if required → terbutaline
questions.exp: Stop oxytocin, turn mother to left lateral, O2 by mask, IV fluids if required, terbutaline (uterine relaxant). (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Precipitate labour is defined as completion of the entire labour in ______ and its consequences include ______.
questions.exp: Precipitate labour: entire process <3 h → perineal tear, hematoma, PPH. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Hypotonic contractions lead to ______ and are managed by ______.
opts: Prolonged/slow progress of labour; augmentation with ARM and oxytocin
questions.exp: Hypotonic contractions → slow progress; augment with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: The instrument for artificial rupture of membranes is ______, identified by ______.
opts: Kocher's forceps; single tooth, multiple rat-like teeth, ratchet lock and transverse serrations
questions.exp: ARM instrument = Kocher's forceps: single tooth, multiple rat-like teeth, ratchet lock, transverse serrations. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Principle of ARM: rupture of membranes → release of ______ → augmentation of labour.
questions.exp: Rupture of membranes releases PGE2 which augments labour. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Absolute contraindications to ARM are:
opts: Maternal HIV, genital herpes infection, IUD of fetus
questions.exp: Absolute C/I: maternal HIV, genital herpes, IUD of fetus. Relative: polyhydramnios (↑ abruption risk) – controlled rupture with slow release. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: In abruptio placentae, ARM is beneficial because it:
opts: Confirms the diagnosis and accelerates the process of labour
questions.exp: ARM in abruptio placenta confirms diagnosis and accelerates labour. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Indication for augmentation is slow progress (dilatation <1 cm/hr in active phase). Sequence when head engaged vs not engaged:
opts: Engaged: ARM → 30 min → oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ cord prolapse risk)
Engaged: oxytocin → ARM; not engaged: ARM → oxytocin
Both: ARM immediately followed by oxytocin
questions.exp: Head engaged: ARM then oxytocin after 30 min; head not engaged: oxytocin first, then ARM to avoid cord prolapse. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Arrange the cardinal movements of labour in order:
opts: Engagement → descent → flexion → internal rotation & crowning → extension → external rotation (restitution) → expulsion
Descent → engagement → extension → flexion → internal rotation → expulsion → restitution
Engagement → flexion → descent → extension → internal rotation → restitution → expulsion
Flexion → engagement → descent → crowning → internal rotation → expulsion → extension
questions.exp: Engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation & crowning, extension, external rotation (restitution), expulsion. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: The prerequisites for a normal delivery are ______ lie, ______ presentation and ______ presenting part.
questions.exp: Normal delivery: longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, vertex presenting part; head usually in LOT (LOT > LOA). (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Internal rotation: the occiput rotates by ______ of a circle at the level of ______, contributed as ______ by neck and ______ by shoulders.
questions.exp: Occiput rotates 2/8th of a circle (90°) at the ischial spine level: 45° by neck + 45° by shoulders. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Crowning is defined as:
opts: Head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions (episiotomy only if required)
Descent of head onto levator ani
Delivery of the head by extension
questions.exp: Crowning = head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions; episiotomy given only if required. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Match – Restitution : External rotation.
opts: Untwisting of neck : shoulder rotates by 1/8th of a circle, visible as head rotates (occiput back to LOT)
Extension of head : flexion of head
questions.exp: Restitution = untwisting of neck; external rotation = shoulders rotate 1/8th of a circle, seen as head rotation (occiput in LOT). (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: WHO recommended methods to prevent perineal tear:
opts: Perineal massage, warm towel at perineum, support perineum with hand, flex head initially then extend for delivery
Routine episiotomy, fundal pressure, early pushing
questions.exp: Perineal massage, warm towel, hand support of perineum, initial flexion then extension of head. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Engagement is defined as the ______ crossing the ______; it occurs at ______ in primigravida and ______ in multigravida.
opts: Largest transverse diameter (biparietal) of head; pelvic inlet; 38 wks; time of labour
questions.exp: Engagement = biparietal diameter crosses pelvic inlet; primi 38 wks, multi at labour. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Signs of engagement – on P/A : on P/V.
questions.exp: P/A ≤2/5 palpable; P/V station 0. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Causes of non-engagement in a primigravida at term, in order of frequency:
opts: Deflexed head (m/c) > CPD > placenta previa; others – polyhydramnios, wrong dates
questions.exp: Deflexed head (m/c) > cephalopelvic disproportion > placenta previa; also polyhydramnios and wrong dates. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Before P/V examination in a primigravida with a free-floating head, ______ must be ruled out; engagement rules out ______.
opts: Placenta previa; CPD at the level of inlet
questions.exp: Rule out placenta previa before P/V in primigravida with free floating head; engagement rules out CPD at the inlet. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Match degree of flexion → presenting part → engaging AP diameter: Fully flexed : Deflexed : Partially extended : Fully extended.
opts: Vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic : vertex/occipito-frontal 11.5 cm : brow/mento-vertical → C-section : face/submento-vertical & submento-bregmatic
questions.exp: Fully flexed vertex – sub-occipitobregmatic; deflexed vertex – occipito-frontal 11.5 cm; brow – mento-vertical (C-section); face – submento-vertical/submento-bregmatic. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: Synclitic engagement means the sagittal suture lies in the transverse diameter of the pelvis:
opts: Midway between pubic symphysis and sacral promontory (LOT position)
In the AP diameter of the pelvis
questions.exp: Synclitic: sagittal suture midway between pubic symphysis and sacral promontory. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: In ANTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards the ______, giving a ______ presentation, with ______ prognosis.
questions.exp: Anterior asynclitism: sagittal suture towards sacrum, anterior parietal presentation, better prognosis. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: In POSTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards ______ and the presentation is ______.
questions.exp: Posterior asynclitism: suture deflected towards pubic symphysis, posterior parietal presentation. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: The head of the baby is delivered by ______ in vertex and by ______ in breech/face.
questions.exp: Vertex – head delivered by extension; breech/face – by flexion. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Pain during the 1st stage arises from ______ (T10–L1) plus ______ (S2–S4).
questions.exp: 1st stage: uterine contractions (T10–L1) + cervical dilatation (S2–S4). (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Pain during the 2nd stage is from cervical dilatation (S2–S4) plus stretching of the perineum via the ______ nerve (______).
questions.exp: 2nd stage: cervical dilatation S2–S4 + perineal stretch via pudendal nerve (S2–S4). (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Epidural analgesia in labour – level of block : type of block.
opts: T10 segment : sensory + sympathetic (no motor block)
questions.exp: Level T10; sensory + sympathetic block without motor block. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Drugs of choice for labour epidural and its effect on stages of labour:
opts: Bupivacaine 0.625% or ropivacaine; shortens 1st stage, prolongs 2nd stage by 1 hr
questions.exp: DOC: bupivacaine (0.625%) / ropivacaine; shortens 1st stage, prolongs 2nd stage by 1 h. Monitor BP and FHR. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Contraindication to epidural and the fact about C-section rate:
opts: Anticoagulant use 12–24 hrs prior to onset of labour; epidural does not increase C-section rate
questions.exp: C/I: anticoagulants within 12–24 h; epidural does not ↑ C-section rate. For C-section, anaesthesia is given at T4 (blocks peritoneal pain). (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Pudendal nerve block – site : ligament pierced : stage of pain relieved.
questions.exp: Pudendal block at ischial spine, piercing sacrospinous ligament, relieves 2nd stage pain. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses of pudendal block are ______; it does NOT block pain during ______.
opts: Instrumental delivery and repair of perineal/vaginal tear; repair of cervical tears
questions.exp: Uses: instrumental delivery, perineal/vaginal tear repair; does not cover cervical tear repair. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Paracervical block – sites : sites avoided (and why) : duration.
opts: 2 or 4 o'clock and 8 or 10 o'clock : 3 and 9 o'clock (descending cervical artery) : 1–2 hrs
questions.exp: Sites 2/4 and 8/10 o'clock; avoid 3 and 9 o'clock because of the descending cervical artery; lasts 1–2 h. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses and contraindication of paracervical block:
opts: Repair of cervix and suction & evacuation; contraindicated in labour as it causes fetal bradycardia
questions.exp: Uses: cervical repair, suction evacuation; not used in labour (fetal bradycardia). (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Prostaglandins act on ______ receptors present on ______ and are released ______.
opts: G-protein cell membrane; myometrium and cervix; locally (paracrine)
questions.exp: G-protein coupled membrane receptors on myometrium and cervix; local paracrine release. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Match prostaglandin synthesis site to product and action – Decidua & myometrium : Amnion.
questions.exp: Decidua/myometrium → PGF2α (uterine action); amnion → PGE2 (cervical action). (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses of prostaglandins in obstetrics include induction (sweeping fingers in internal os releases PGE2 → cervical ripening), and:
opts: Augmentation of labour and management of PPH
questions.exp: Uses: induction, augmentation of labour, management of PPH. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Induction of labour (IOL) is defined as ______; Bishop score checks ______ with a maximum of ______.
opts: Initiation of uterine contractions in a patient not in labour; readiness of cervix and uterus before IOL; 13
Acceleration of established labour; fetal wellbeing; 10
Artificial rupture of membranes; pelvic adequacy; 9
questions.exp: IOL = initiation of contractions in a patient not in labour; Bishop score assesses cervix/uterus readiness; maximum 13. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Match the mnemonic 'Delhi Police Employed Special Commanders' to Bishop parameters:
opts: Dilation, Presentation, Effacement, Softness, Cervix length
questions.exp: Delhi = dilation, Police = position, Employed = effacement, Special = station, Commanders = consistency. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for DILATION of cervix (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):
questions.exp: Dilation: closed 0; 1–2 cm 1; 3–4 cm 2; >5 cm 3 – the most important parameter. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for POSITION of cervix (0 : 1 : 2) and its importance:
opts: Posterior : middle : anterior; least important parameter
questions.exp: Position: posterior 0, middle 1, anterior 2; least important parameter. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for EFFACEMENT (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for STATION of fetal head (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):
questions.exp: Station: above −2 = 0; −2 = 1; −1/0 = 2; below ischial spine = 3. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for CONSISTENCY (0 : 1 : 2):
questions.exp: Consistency: firm 0, mid 1, soft 2. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: The simplified Bishop score uses ______ with a maximum of ______; the modified Bishop score replaces ______ with ______.
opts: Dilation, effacement, station; 9; placement (position) of cervix; length of cervix by USG
Dilation, position, consistency; 7; station; fetal weight
questions.exp: Simplified: dilation + effacement + station (max 9). Modified: position replaced by USG cervical length. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Interpretation of Bishop score – ≤5 : ≥6 : ≥9.
opts: Cervix not ripe, IOL unlikely to succeed : favourable for IOL : chances of vaginal delivery similar to spontaneous labour
questions.exp: ≤5 unripe (IOL will not succeed); ≥6 favourable; ≥9 vaginal delivery chances similar to spontaneous labour. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Match the methods – Cervical ripening : IOL : Augmentation.
opts: Sweeping of membranes, mechanical, prostaglandins : mechanical, prostaglandins, oxytocin : oxytocin, ARM
Prostaglandins only : ARM only : oxytocin only
questions.exp: Ripening: sweeping, mechanical, PGs. IOL: mechanical, PGs, oxytocin. Augmentation: oxytocin, ARM. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Sweeping (stripping) of membranes – indication and principle:
opts: Cervix slightly dilated; sweeping detaches membranes from cervix → release of prostaglandins → ripening
questions.exp: Indication: slightly dilated cervix; membranes detached from cervix → PG release → cervical ripening. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Mechanical methods of IOL both ripen the cervix and induce labour; they are preferred in:
questions.exp: Mechanical methods ripen + induce and are preferred in a scarred uterus. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Transcervical Foley catheter for IOL – size, placement and volume:
opts: No. 16 in endocervical canal, bulb seated at internal os, inflated with 30 ml NS → cervical stretching → PG release
No. 12 in vagina, bulb at external os, 10 ml
questions.exp: No. 16 Foley inserted into endocervical canal; bulb at level of internal os; 30 ml NS → stretching of cervix → prostaglandins. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Extra-amniotic saline infusion (EASI) involves:
opts: Foley in endocervical canal with bulb inflated and NS infused at 30–40 ml/hr; saline collects in extra-amniotic space → separation of membranes → PG release
Infusion of saline into the amniotic cavity via amniocentesis
questions.exp: EASI: NS 30–40 ml/hr via Foley → collects between amnion/chorion and uterus → membrane separation → prostaglandins. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Hygroscopic dilators used for IOL are exemplified by:
questions.exp: Hygroscopic dilator = laminaria tent. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Prostaglandins for IOL are contraindicated in ______; risk of tachysystole ranks ______.
questions.exp: PG C/I: scarred uterus. Tachysystole: Cervidil > Cerviprime > misoprostol. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Misoprostol (PGE1) for IOL – dose, repetition, maximum and next step:
opts: 25 mcg oral/vaginal repeated 3–6 hourly (4 h), max 6 doses; if no IOL after a 4 h gap → oxytocin
50 mcg vaginal 2 hourly, max 4 doses → C-section
questions.exp: 25 mcg orally/vaginally every 3–6 h (4 h), maximum 6 doses; no labour → 4 h gap → oxytocin. S/E: FHR abnormalities, meconium staining. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Cerviprime gel (dinoprostone PGE2) – dose : site : repeat : maximum : storage.
opts: 0.5 mg : into cervix : 6 hourly : 3 doses, then oxytocin after 6 h : refrigerated
10 mg : posterior fornix : once : 1 : room temperature
questions.exp: Cerviprime 0.5 mg intracervical, 6-hourly, max 3 doses (oxytocin 6 h after last), refrigerated. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Cervidil (dinoprostone insert) – dose : release rate : site : duration.
opts: 10 mg : 0.3 mg/hr : posterior fornix : kept 12 h until labour
questions.exp: Cervidil 10 mg releasing 0.3 mg/hr, placed in posterior fornix, kept up to 12 h. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Oxytocin for IOL – if cervix is ripe ______; if not ripe ______.
opts: Use oxytocin directly; ripen cervix then oxytocin
questions.exp: Ripe cervix → oxytocin directly; unripe → ripen then oxytocin. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Standard oxytocin infusion for IOL:
opts: 5 U in 500 ml NS = 10 mIU/ml = 0.5 mIU/drop; max 52 drops/min (26 mIU/min)
10 U in 500 ml = 20 mIU/ml; max 20 drops/min
5 U in 100 ml = 50 mIU/ml; max 10 drops
2 U in 1 L = 2 mIU/ml; max 100 drops
questions.exp: 5 U oxytocin + 500 ml NS → 10 mIU/ml → 0.5 mIU/drop; maximum 52 drops/min = 26 mIU/min. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Side effects of oxytocin infusion:
opts: Water intoxication/hyponatremia if dissolved in 5% dextrose; hypotension if drop rate ↑
questions.exp: Water intoxication (hyponatremia) with 5% dextrose; hypotension with rapid rate. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL is contraindicated wherever vaginal delivery is contraindicated. Which is NOT on the list?
opts: Malpresentation – transverse lie, brow, mentoposterior face
Active genital herpes / contracted pelvis / CPD / cancer cervix
questions.exp: Listed: placenta previa, vasa previa, malpresentation, active herpes, contracted pelvis, CPD, cancer cervix, previous classical C-section/myomectomy, fetal distress, mono-mono/conjoined twins. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: Which prior surgical histories contraindicate IOL?
questions.exp: Previous classical C-section or myomectomy contraindicate IOL. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: Which twin situations contraindicate IOL?
questions.exp: MCMA twins and conjoined twins are C/I to IOL, as is fetal distress. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL in a scarred uterus:
questions.exp: Scarred uterus: mechanical ripening followed by oxytocin (PGs contraindicated). (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL for IUD of fetus – 20–28 weeks : >28 weeks.
opts: Misoprostol 600–800 mcg PV, repeat 400 mcg 3-hourly : 25 mg misoprostol to ripen cervix → oxytocin
questions.exp: 20–28 wks: misoprostol 600–800 mcg PV then 400 mcg 3-hourly; >28 wks: 25 mg misoprostol (ripen) → oxytocin. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Third stage of labour – main factor affecting placental separation : plane of separation : m/c method of separation.
opts: Uterine contractions : zona spongiosa : Schultz method
Cord traction : zona basalis : Duncan method
questions.exp: Separation depends on uterine contractions, occurs through zona spongiosa, m/c Schultz method. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: The surest sign of placental separation is:
opts: Placenta felt in vagina (> apparent and permanent lengthening of cord)
questions.exp: Surest sign = placenta felt in vagina > permanent lengthening of cord. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Passive management of the third stage (not preferred) involves:
opts: Waiting for spontaneous expulsion (about 15 min) → ↑ blood loss → ↑ PPH and maternal mortality
questions.exp: Passive: wait for spontaneous expulsion (~15 min) → ↑ blood loss, PPH and mortality. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Advantages and drawback of AMTSL:
opts: ↓ duration (5–10 min), ↓ blood loss, best method to prevent PPH, ↓ maternal mortality; drawback ↑ chance of retained placenta (use of uterotonics)
questions.exp: AMTSL: 3rd stage 5–10 min, ↓ blood loss, best PPH prevention, ↓ mortality; drawback ↑ retained placenta. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Arrange the four steps of AMTSL:
opts: Uterotonic within 1 min of delivery (or at delivery of anterior shoulder) → delayed cord clamping → controlled cord traction → intermittent assessment of uterine tone
Early cord clamping → uterotonic → traction → tone
questions.exp: 1 uterotonic <1 min; 2 delayed cord clamping; 3 controlled cord traction; 4 intermittent uterine tone assessment. Uterine massage (former 4th step) is now PPH treatment; early clamping not done. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: WHO-recommended uterotonic for AMTSL – dose, route, storage:
opts: Oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV infusion (in RL/NS); stored at 2–8 °C
Oxytocin 5 IU IV bolus; room temperature
questions.exp: Oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV infusion; stored 2–8 °C. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Oxytocin IV bolus is contraindicated because it causes ______; 5% dextrose preparation causes ______.
opts: Hypotension, tachycardia, arrhythmias, cardiac arrest; water intoxication (anti-diuretic effect)
questions.exp: IV bolus → hypotension, tachycardia, arrhythmia, arrest; dextrose 5% → water intoxication. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: If oxytocin is unavailable, methylergometrine is given as:
opts: 0.2 mg IM (IV avoided due to severe hypertension); stored at room temperature
questions.exp: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM (IV causes severe hypertension), stored at room temperature. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Syntometrine is a fixed combination of ______ with the advantage of ______ but disadvantage of ______.
opts: 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg methylergometrine; ↑ efficacy; expensive and ↓ availability
10 U oxytocin + 0.2 mg ME; cheap; hypertension
5 U oxytocin + 250 mcg carboprost; long action; bronchospasm
0.5 mg ME + 600 mcg misoprostol; oral; fever
questions.exp: Syntometrine = 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg ME; more efficacious but expensive/less available. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Carbetocin (synthetic oxytocin octapeptide) – dose, half-life and restriction:
opts: 100 mcg slow IV over 1 min; t½ 40 min (oxytocin 3–5 min); action 3 h; not used for induction/augmentation or PPH management
250 mcg IM; t½ 5 min; used for PPH
10 IU IM; t½ 20 min; used for induction
1 mg IV; t½ 60 min; PPH treatment
questions.exp: Carbetocin 100 mcg slow IV; t½ 40 min vs 3–5 min for oxytocin; lasts 3 h; not for IOL/augmentation or PPH treatment. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Misoprostol (PGE1) as a uterotonic in AMTSL is dosed:
questions.exp: Misoprost 600 mcg orally/sublingually (400–600 mcg). (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Type of contraction – oxytocin : methylergometrine.
opts: Physiological, regular intervals with relaxation (allows fetal blood flow) : tetanic, no relaxation (may cause fetal distress)
questions.exp: Oxytocin: physiological contractions with relaxation; ME: tetanic without relaxation. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Site of action and use – oxytocin : methylergometrine.
opts: Lower and upper segments; IOL, augmentation, preferred for AMTSL : mainly lower segment; only after delivery of baby, not first line in AMTSL (↑ retained placenta)
Lower segment; PPH only : both segments; IOL
Upper only; IOL : upper only; AMTSL first line
questions.exp: Oxytocin acts on both segments and is preferred for AMTSL; ME acts mainly on LUS, given only after delivery and not first line (retained placenta). (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Complication – oxytocin : methylergometrine.
questions.exp: Oxytocin bolus → hypotension; ME → hypertension. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Carboprost/dinoprostone (PGF2α) and tranexamic acid in the third stage are:
opts: Not used in AMTSL – reserved for PPH management; if ↑ PPH risk, 1 g tranexamic acid IV in 100 ml NS over 20 min + oxytocin
questions.exp: Carboprost/PGF2α and tranexamic acid are reserved for PPH; high-risk women get 1 g TXA IV over 20 min + oxytocin. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Dinoprostone (PGE2) is used for ______ but is NOT recommended by WHO for ______.
opts: Induction and augmentation of labour; AMTSL and PPH management
questions.exp: PGE2: IOL/augmentation; not recommended for AMTSL or PPH. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) means clamping at ______ and is included in ______.
opts: ≥1 min (1–3 min); Anemia Mukt Bharat programme
questions.exp: DCC ≥1 min (1–3 min), part of Anemia Mukt Bharat. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Advantage of DCC:
opts: ≈80 ml extra cord blood (~50 mg elemental iron) to baby → prevents neonatal anemia
questions.exp: 80 ml extra blood ≈ 50 mg elemental iron → prevents neonatal anemia. Indicated in all deliveries including preterm, post-term, maternal COVID-19. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Absolute indication for early cord clamping (ECC):
opts: Need for neonatal resuscitation (e.g., birth asphyxia)
questions.exp: Absolute: need for neonatal resuscitation. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Relative indications for ECC include all EXCEPT:
opts: Rh-negative mother with negative ICT (if ICT positive → DCC)
questions.exp: Relative ECC: Rh-negative mother ± ICT negative, fetal heart disease, excessive maternal bleeding. COVID-19 is an indication FOR DCC. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: HIV-positive mothers – WHO/ACOG : national guidelines; and what reduces vertical transmission more?
opts: DCC : ECC after cessation of cord pulsations; ART > ECC
questions.exp: WHO/ACOG recommend DCC; Indian guidelines ECC after pulsations cease; ART reduces transmission more than ECC. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Step 3 of AMTSL uses the technique of ______ (a.k.a. ______) performed by ______.
opts: Controlled cord traction; modified Brandt-Andrews technique; skilled birth attendant
Credé's method; fundal expression; any attendant
questions.exp: CCT = modified Brandt-Andrews technique, by a skilled birth attendant; Credé's method is outdated. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Correct procedure of controlled cord traction:
opts: Look for signs of separation → push uterus upwards with one hand → gentle downward-forward traction on cord during contraction
Pull cord continuously regardless of separation
Traction between contractions with fundal pressure
questions.exp: Signs of separation → counter-pressure pushing uterus up → gentle traction downwards and forwards during contraction. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: If the cord breaks during CCT, management is:
opts: Manual removal of placenta under general anaesthesia using a sweeping hand in the plane between uterus and placenta
questions.exp: Cord snap → manual removal under GA with sweeping action between uterus and placenta. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Pulling the cord before the placenta has separated risks ______; failure to find a plane between placenta and uterus suggests ______.
opts: Uterine inversion; morbidly adherent placenta (placenta accreta spectrum)
questions.exp: Premature traction → uterine inversion; no cleavage plane → placenta accreta spectrum. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Persistent bleeding after placental delivery with a retained part of placenta on USG suggests:
questions.exp: Retained lobe → placenta succenturiata or bilobata. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Step 4 – intermittent assessment of uterine tone is done every ______ for ______; retained placenta/prolonged third stage is defined as placenta undelivered ______ after birth.
questions.exp: Tone every 15 min for 1–2 h; retained placenta = not delivered ≥30 min after baby. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Fourth stage of labour – duration, a normal maternal experience and monitoring intervals:
opts: 1–2 hrs after placenta; physiological chills; uterine tone, pulse, BP every 15 min, temperature every 4 hrs
questions.exp: 4th stage 1–2 h; physiological chills; tone/pulse/BP every 15 min, temp every 4 h. (Book p527)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Advice given in the fourth stage and its possible complications:
opts: Pass urine and take oral intake within 2 h of delivery; PPH, perineal tears, vulval hematomas
Nil by mouth for 6 h; uterine rupture
questions.exp: Advice: pass urine and oral intake within 2 h; complications PPH, perineal tears, vulval hematoma. (Book p527)

units.title: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
units.guide: Define normal labour by its five criteria and walk through the four uterine phases from quiescence to postpartum with their hormonal drivers. Focus for this checkpoint: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour.

units.title: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
units.guide: Recognise lightening, false pains and the biochemistry of cervical ripening, then separate true from false labour pain across six features. Focus for this checkpoint: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain.

units.title: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
units.guide: Quantify the origin, speed, pressure thresholds and stage-wise strengths of contractions, and understand Montevideo units and segment formation. Focus for this checkpoint: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions.

units.title: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
units.guide: Define tachysystole and precipitate labour with their causes and consequences, and manage hypertonic and hypotonic uterine activity. Focus for this checkpoint: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions.

units.title: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
units.guide: Identify Kocher's forceps, the prostaglandin logic of ARM, its absolute and relative contraindications, and the engaged/unengaged sequencing rule. Focus for this checkpoint: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence.

units.title: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
units.guide: Order the seven cardinal movements and know the degree of rotation, the definition of crowning, restitution and WHO perineal protection steps. Focus for this checkpoint: Cardinal movements & the process of labour.

units.title: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
units.guide: Define engagement by the biparietal diameter, its clinical signs, why a primigravida's head may float at term and which AP diameter engages in each attitude. Focus for this checkpoint: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters.

units.title: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
units.guide: Distinguish synclitic from anterior and posterior asynclitic engagement by where the sagittal suture points, and recall how the head is delivered in vertex vs breech/face. Focus for this checkpoint: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement.

units.title: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
units.guide: Trace the spinal segments carrying 1st and 2nd stage pain, and set the level, drugs, effects, monitoring and contraindication of epidural analgesia. Focus for this checkpoint: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia.

units.title: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
units.guide: Locate the pudendal and paracervical block sites, their uses and hazards, then cover prostaglandin receptors, synthesis sites and obstetric uses. Focus for this checkpoint: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins.

units.title: Induction of labour: Bishop score
units.guide: Score every Bishop parameter with the DELHI POLICE mnemonic, know the most and least important items, the simplified and modified versions, and interpret the totals. Focus for this checkpoint: Induction of labour: Bishop score.

units.title: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
units.guide: Group the ripening, induction and augmentation methods, then detail membrane sweeping, Foley, EASI and laminaria – the options preferred in a scarred uterus. Focus for this checkpoint: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods.

units.title: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
units.guide: Dose misoprostol, cerviprime gel and Cervidil correctly, rank their tachysystole risk, and prepare and titrate oxytocin safely. Focus for this checkpoint: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction.

units.title: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
units.guide: Recall the ten conditions where vaginal delivery – and hence induction – is contraindicated, and the protocols for scarred uterus and intrauterine death. Focus for this checkpoint: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases.

units.title: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
units.guide: Master placental separation physiology, the signs, passive vs active management and the four steps of AMTSL. Focus for this checkpoint: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview.

units.title: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
units.guide: Dose and store oxytocin, methylergometrine, syntometrine, carboprost and misoprostol, and contrast oxytocin with methylergometrine. Focus for this checkpoint: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives.

units.title: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
units.guide: Time delayed clamping, its iron benefit and programme link, and list every absolute and relative indication for early clamping including the HIV nuance. Focus for this checkpoint: Step 2: delayed cord clamping.

units.title: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
units.guide: Perform controlled cord traction correctly, handle the special cases (cord snap, inversion, PAS, succenturiate lobe), then run fourth-stage monitoring. Focus for this checkpoint: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage.
